description.narrative: Following the sharp escalation of hostilities in Lebanon, the Ministry of Public Health has recorded over 450 deaths, 1,313 injuries, and around 667,831 IDPs as of March 9th. Beirut and Mount Lebanon (BML) and the South governorates are among the areas most affected by displacement. Around 119,700 IDPS are now hosted in 567 collective shelters, many located in Chouf (BML) and Saida and Sour (South), and most of which are public schools that were operating at capacity. Plan and partners’ ongoing response shows shortages of bedding, hygiene kits (especially in Chouf). Protection concerns are increasing in overcrowded shelter environments where women and girls report feeling unsafe, psychosocial distress is rising, and WASH services are strained, especially affecting children, older persons, and PwDs. The economic crisis has weakened public institutions’ response to the scale of needs. Food insecurity is worsening with displacement disrupting livelihoods. Humanitarian support is required to address immediate needs for displaced populations. PIL, with SHEILD and DPNA, will scale up its existing distributions of hygiene and MHM kits as well as food assistance in collective shelters, with protection mainstreamed across all activities.

PIL will implement with its long-standing partners DPNA, who will implement in Saida (South) and Chouf (Mount Lebanon), and SHEILD, who will implement in Sour (South). Partners have been engaged in the needs identification and interventions design, ensuring that emerging needs and access considerations of the targeted populations are reflected. The action will build on Plan’s ongoing response, which has reached 12,000 beneficiaries through WASH and FSL distributions since March 2nd. PIL will directly implement activities in hard-to-reach areas in the South, building on its strong coordination with UNOCHA and experience facilitating access there. Since the escalation of recent hostilities, PIL has supported the deployment of a convoy there and will be responsible for implementation to ensure timely provision of assistance where partner access is limited. PIL will provide technical and coordination support and operational resources to ensure that partners are supported to deliver timely and quality response. The partners will receive 74% of the budget (incl. 6% ICR each), divided based on needs. In line with the Joint Response framework, PIL coordinated with various UN, local and international organizations and DRA members such as Oxfam, War Child, World Vision, Dorcas, and CARE to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication of services and maximize impact, which will be continued primarily through the centralised systems in place.

Plan’s emergency response plan is currently being implemented through Plan’s Ready to Respond approach. DRA funding will allow an immediate scale-up using Plan, DPNA and SHEILD’s existing infrastructure and procurement processes including Long-Term Agreements in place with suppliers. Distribution can start immediately, building on 12,000 beneficiaries already reached with distributions since March 2nd. 24 specific shelters are already selected (see LF). Areas of implementation were selected based on humanitarian needs and lessons learned from the 2024 DRA response, when a ceasefire during implementation did not result in IDPs returning home. Priority is to ensure timely and sustained assistance to populations expected to remain displaced while ensuring that displaced households outside shelters are reached quickly. Implementation will mostly be completed in the first 2 months, similar to the 2024 ACJR when Plan and DPNA distributed 80% of activities in the first 1,5 month.

SUMMARY: In response to the escalation of hostilities in Lebanon in March 2026, which resulted in a massive influx of displacement and causalities, Dutch Relief Alliance (DRA) has launched an acute joint response. Plan International Netherlands, as a member partner of DRA JR in Lebanon, and in collaboration with Plan Lebanon and local partners, are jointly responding in Beirut and Mount Lebanon (BML) and the South governorates, as they are among the areas most affected by displacement. The intervention is designed to respond to the needs of IDPs living in communities, residential settings and 24 targeted collective shelters. Living conditions and vulnerabilities vary across these contexts. The response will thus apply a tailored, integrated approach aligned with national and cluster coordination mechanisms. Distribution of core relief items, including hygiene, MHM kits, and food parcels in the target areas including hard-to-reach areas, aims to reach a 38,800 unique beneficiaries.

The intervention is designed to respond to the needs of IDPs living in communities, residential settings and 24 targeted collective shelters. The response will thus apply a tailored, integrated approach aligned with national and cluster coordination mechanisms. Distribution of core relief items, including hygiene and MHM kits for 4700 HHs in line with WASH standards while food insecurity will be addressed by distributing 5000 food parcels/RTEs in line with sector guidance. These will be distributed in collective shelters in Sour, Saida and Mount Lebanon by DPNA and SHEILD, and in hard-to-reach areas through convoys directly by Plan. Plan expected to reach 38,800 unique beneficiaries. Protection will be mainstreamed in all activities. Field monitors will conduct regular visits to shelters to monitor protection risks and identify/refer individuals at heightened risk to specialized services. Individuals facing urgent concerns will be referred to PRT/CP/GBV case management services. Psychological First Aid will be integrated across all activities to ensure appropriate support to affected populations. Plan will continue to coordinate its response with other actors and for this project.

The response will target vulnerable Lebanese communities, Palestinian refugees and Syrian refugees through an inclusive and needs-based approach, providing ±80% of assistance to people in displacement (1st, 2nd or more), with a focus on IDPs, refugees & migrants, with attention to political sensitivities surrounding this humanitarian approach. Attention will be given to the most vulnerable households and individuals. Based on previous RNA’s and the partners’ experience implementing the emergency response in Lebanon, these groups include Children and youth, unaccompanied and separated minors, SGBV survivors, women and girls at risk of sexual exploitation and trafficking, Female-headed households, Working children, Older persons (especially women), Persons with functional diversity, and pregnant and lactating women. The extensive protection mainstreaming and collaborative identification processes will enable the partners to provide tailored assistance to these groups.
